what: FastScan 1-bit SIMD sign kernel for theodb_symqg (plan symqg-fastscan-1bit). Two measurements on ONE dedicated c-8 droplet (no CPU steal): (1) primary A/B theodb_symqg v3 FastScan vs theodb_hnsw at matched recall; (2) ablation FastScan ON vs OFF (SET theodb.symqg_fastscan) on the SAME index — isolates the kernel's effect (the v2-vs-v3 cross-box comparison was confounded by the box change).
hardware: DigitalOcean c-8 (8 vCPU CPU-Optimized DEDICATED, no steal), PostgreSQL 17.10 + pgrx 0.19.0, shared_buffers=2GB
gate: theodb_symqg QPS >= 1.5x theodb_hnsw at matched recall@10 >= 0.95

primary_ab.note: same box, same session; symqg v3 FastScan (default on) vs hnsw

ablation_fastscan_vs_scalar.note: SAME index (built once), SAME box; only the estimate kernel differs (SET theodb.symqg_fastscan). Isolates the FastScan effect + proves recall-neutrality.

verdict: FastScan kernel is CORRECT and RECALL-NEUTRAL (fastscan vs scalar recall identical within 0.1 pp across the sweep; int8 requant preserves ranking — D3 gate passed). But the measured FastScan speedup is MODEST: 1.07-1.22x (grows with ef), NOT the 2.4-2.8x a naive v2-vs-v3 cross-box comparison suggested (that was almost entirely the steal→dedicated box change). The gate (symqg >= 1.5x hnsw @ recall>=0.95) is NOT met: theodb_hnsw is 2.1-3.5x faster at matched recall (0.95-0.994), converging to parity only at recall 0.999.
why_modest: The per-hop estimate (32 scalar sign-dots) is NOT the sole bottleneck (Amdahl): row decode (rot 512B + ords + signs + nr/w), the beam-search heap ops, the HashSet visited-set, and the page reads together dominate more than the estimate. Accelerating only the estimate ~4-8x yields ~1.2x overall — the same 'assumed bottleneck != whole story' lesson as E1 (WARM Stage-2) and E2 (page tax). The mature theodb_hnsw AM (M35-M46: copy-free reads, SIMD distance, lean neighbour hop) remains faster.
honesty_note: The v2-vs-v3 speedup MUST NOT be quoted from the two separate-box runs (v2 on a steal-heavy shared box, v3 on a dedicated c-8): hnsw itself went 287->712 QPS purely from the box change. The same-index ablation is the only honest FastScan measurement. No symqg QPS-win-over-hnsw claim is made (public-copy.md, rule 5).
correctness: theodb_symqg v3 (block32-nibble layout, FastScan dispatch D5 with scalar fallback for dim>1032) is functionally correct: CREATE INDEX / scan / recall preserved on real SIFT1M; the D5 eligibility dispatch protects 1536-dim OpenAI embeddings from int16 overflow (scalar fallback). Only the QPS gate is unmet.
